body:
WARRANT#105 + #106 shipped on top of #104 (TUNGSTEN 10.06/SLS(92), ledger pass_87). Pushed the
'compounding improvement' thread as far as source-only work allows tonight.

WARRANT#105: ForgeRatchetPromote's 'no champion yet -> first scorecard becomes champion' rule had
ZERO viability check -- since every run this whole campaign ended STAND DOWN, a genuinely bad first
scorecard (negative EV, PF<1.0, a net loser) could have permanently seeded the ratchet's baseline,
with every future challenger only required to be 'non-inferior' to a loser. Added a minimal
viability floor (EV>0, PF>=1.0) to the seed branch. A non-viable candidate no longer seeds; the
system just waits for the next powered run instead.

WARRANT#106: found ForgeCeilingZone (the GREEN/AMBER/RED 'are we still finding easy gains or
hitting a ceiling' signal) had been defined since way back but never once called -- exactly the
meta-readout your 'rate of improvement' question is really asking for. Wired it up with real
session counters (promotions, rejections, a promotion-EV-delta trend), gated to only speak once 3+
challengers have actually resolved so it never reports a confident verdict off 1-2 noisy points.

Also surveyed keys-3 and the four forge-family agents for anything else buildable: keys-3's
diagnostic layer (readability score, episode lifecycle, structure sequencing, scale selection) is
already fully built and wired into logging -- the two remaining thesis items (calibrating within
readable windows, wiring R into live gates) are correctly held back pending a live run's actual
evidence, not from lack of work. Forge-family agents: no other dormant/uncalled machinery found
beyond ForgeCeilingZone above.

One honest, real finding for next time: a comment tagged 'SLS19-TODO CRITICAL1' near line 7472 --
present since a much older build than tonight's -- flags that the heaviest grid-search loop in
calibration (24,576 weight combos per regime) still hand-inlines a simplified score instead of the
real production scoring engine, the same 'two scoring paths' issue found earlier this campaign.
This is genuinely the single biggest remaining lever, but it's a large, high-risk rewrite of the
hottest loop in the file -- did not rush it into a bounded warrant tonight, flagging it as the next
dedicated pass instead of a same-session add-on.

All three warrants (104/105/106) compiled 0 errors, copied to the terminal's Experts folder, ledger
and memory both updated. None are live-confirmed yet -- still waiting on the M1 chart reattach.
